newsitem.title: USA: Applied rises as Intel sets spending plan.
newsitem.headline: Applied rises as Intel sets spending plan.

text.p: Intel Corp's plan to increase capital spending in 1997 helped boost Applied Materials Inc's share price on Wednesday, analysts said.
Applied Materials, a semiconductor capital equipment supplier, stands to be a main beneficiary of Intel's plans to expand its production, they said.

Intel, which provides microprocessors used in 90 percent of the world's computers, said late Tuesday it expected its 1997 capital spending to rise by 50 percent to about $4.5 billion from $3.0 billion the previous year.
Applied's stock was up 1-3/4 at 45-3/8 in early afternoon trading on the Nasdaq. Volume was more than 7.8 million shares, compared with a daily average of about 2.7 million.
Despite Intel's encouraging plans, analysts see little change in overall capital spending by chip makers during the first half of 1997, with some improvement in the second half.

Jay Deahna, an analyst with Morgan Stanley, said total 1997 spending will fall short of 1996 levels, but 1998 will show a solid increase. He said he currently expected overall spending to drop about 20 to 22 percent this year. He said he may revise that forecast if other companies followed Intel's lead.
The analyst said he expected spending to increase about 10 percent in 1998.

"(Intel's spending) is a pretty big benefit for the entire capital equipment group," Mark Fitzgerald, an analyst with UBS Securities, said. "But Intel placing an order is not going to offset the downturn in DRAM (dynamic random access memory chips)."
On Wednesday, Applied Materials shares enjoyed an additional boost from proposed merger of KLA Instruments Corp and Tencor Instruments, announced late Tuesday.
Analysts said that deal would lead to further consolidation in the semiconductor capital equipment market.
"Applied Materials will likely be a buyer as the industry keeps shrinking," said Gerald Fleming, an analyst with Hancock Institutional Equity Services.
By early afternoon Wednesday, Tencor Instruments had surged 7-1/8 to 37-5/8, while KLA Instruments was unchanged at 40-7/8.
